title: Introduce profile stitcher and consolidated release glossary for onboarding
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: When onboarding models we've repeatedly seen fragmented performance and affordance metadata across variants (quantization, hardware target, tokenizer differences) which makes release notes noisy and causes regressions to be under- or over-emphasized. This PR introduces a 'profile stitcher' that merges variant-level profiles into a canonical composite profile using provenance-weighted heuristics and conflict-resolution rules; it also adds a release glossary/annotation generator to the changelog pipeline to produce consolidated, severity-tagged release notes and a short glossary of terms introduced by a model (affordances, profiler metrics, and hardware-specific caveats). Implementation summary: 1) registry/onboard/stitcher.py implements a stitcher core that groups profiles by affinity keys, computes weighted medians for numeric metrics, and preserves per-variant provenance tags; 2) tools/changelog/generator.go gains a new pipeline stage that consumes composite profiles to emit release annotations (severity: info/warn/critical) and an auto-generated glossary.md fragment for each release; 3) API: POST /onboard/preview now returns both the composite profile and a previewed release-glossary blob for review in Console; 4) CLI: added rs-onboard preview-glossary command to let curators inspect suggested annotations locally; 5) tests: integration tests exercise stitcher heuristics across synthetic variant sets and end-to-end changelog generation; 6) docs: docs/registry/release-glossary.md explains glossary semantics and guidance for curators. Backwards compatibility: the stitcher is opt-in behind registry.onboard.stitch.enabled=false by default for rollout, and existing per-variant profiles are left unchanged in the store. Related work: ties to ENG-4921 (profile canonicalization) and ENG-4999 (changelog automation). Rollout plan: feature gated for 2 weeks with canary sampling (5% of onboards), UI preview enabled for curated reviewers, then enable default merge after metrics show no regressions.
